turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Mr. Hale. Thank you for seeing me.

I have twenty minutes. Then a client call.

Owen got a zero. Fifteen percent of his English mark. You entered it before you called me.

I'd like to know why.
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.

I'm a lawyer, Mr. Hale. Words are the job.

That's not why I'm here.

You entered a zero. Before you called me. Walk me through how that happened.
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?

No. Not today.

I'm not your drafter. I'm Owen's mother.

I have nineteen minutes. Let's talk about his essay.

What did the checker actually show you? A score? A report? Show me.
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.

No, Mr. Hale.

Flattery won't change that. Neither will asking twice.

Your cafeteria email is yours to write.

Owen's zero is mine to ask about.

So. The checker. Which tool? What date did you run it? What did it say, exactly?
